    "B can show value on the first install: watch the vendor, diff the change, scan the repo, open a PR. It does not need accumulated history. A's brief says earning gating trust typically takes months of track record, which works directly against a 90-day goal.",
    "Both spaces are crowded, and B has several free competitors. But B's competitors are mostly indie projects at low price points. A faces funded incumbents (Develocity, Harness, BrowserStack) plus a wave of near-identical OSS clones, and A's brief notes the core technique doesn't strictly require an LLM.",
    "Both carry a false-positive/negative trust risk and a risk around granting code access. Neither risk separates them, so the decision rests on the demand, pricing, and cold-start differences above."

The pick rests mainly on B's more independent demand evidence, its SMB-tier price anchors, and its lack of a cold-start barrier. Neither brief establishes a clear edge in differentiation."
